title: Oncall Continuity Accelerator and Retro Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook collects a compact, actionable set of procedures and artifacts for on-call continuity: detecting and triaging incidents, operational runbooks for common inference failures, customer-facing status templates, postmortem sequencing and ownership, on-call rotation best practices, and a reproducible game-day plan for measuring responder readiness. It is designed to be used in-the-bridge and as a living reference during and after incidents.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: shorten time-to-restoration while preserving signal for learning.
- Scope: covers Redwood public inference stack components (inference-router, model-serving, kv-cache, request-orchestrator, auth-proxy, metrics/trace). Private deployments should follow the same lifecycle but may have different SLO thresholds and escalation contacts.

Key roles (definitions):
1) Incident Commander (IC) — owns prioritization, customer comms, and final technical decisions for the incident.
2) Bridge Lead / Bridge Facilitator — runs the bridge, captures timeline, assigns tasks.
3) Primary Responder — engineer(s) actively diagnosing and remediating the service.
4) Secondary Responder / Escalation — on-call senior or specialist (serving-runtime, infra, sre).
5) Communications Lead — writes status updates and coordinates legal/CS briefings if needed.
6) Postmortem Owner — produces the RCA and action items.

Incident lifecycle (high level):
1) Detection and acknowledgement (0 - 5 min):
   - Alerts: PagerDuty triggers for SLO breaches, automated synthetic failures, or customer reports.
   - Triage: first responder acknowledges within 5 minutes. If not acknowledged, escalation to rotation backup.
2) Triage (5 - 20 min):
   - Quick scope: which service(s), region(s), customers impacted? Use dashboards: /dashboards/slo-overview, /dashboards/request-queue, /dashboards/error-rate.
   - Classify impact: P0 (outage with broad customer impact), P1 (partial degradation), P2 (single-customer or degraded non-critical path).
3) Containment (20 - 60 min):
   - Apply safe fallbacks: route traffic to compatible model-variant, enable degraded QoS mode (drop large requests), or scale reserve pool.
   - Short-term mitigations should be reversible and logged.
4) Remediation (1 - 6+ hours):
   - Execute root-cause repairs (bugfix, config rollback, capacity change).
   - Run targeted validation before full cutover.
5) Recovery and verification (post-remediation):
   - Confirm SLOs are back to normal for 30 minutes. Close the incident only after validating customer facing metrics.
6) Post-incident: timeline capture, postmortem draft, action items, and closure.

Triage decision ladder (short):
1) Is traffic failing across all regions? -> escalate to multi-region SRE.
2) Are error rates isolated to a model version? -> rollback model and pin to last known-good version.
3) Is queue length > queue_threshold (see service thresholds table)? -> scale horizontal pool, enable request-drop policy.

Service thresholds (operational quick reference):
| Service | Alert threshold | Immediate action |
| inference-router | 5xx rate > 2% p5m OR latency p95 > 800ms | Failover to alternate route, call IC |
| model-serving | error-rate > 3% p5m OR model-load > 90% GPU | Rollback model, scale pool |
| kv-cache | miss-rate > 20% OR latency p95 > 200ms | Flush selective prefixes, scale cache nodes |
| request-orchestrator | queue-length > 2000 OR processed rate drop > 30% | Apply backpressure, scale consumers |
| auth-proxy | 401/403 spike > baseline +5x | Verify auth PKI, fallback to cached tokens |

(Use the thresholds as guidance; adjust per-customer/region in dedicated/private deployments.)

Example runbook: inference-router high-queue / increased 5xx
1) Detection: alert from /dashboards/request-queue shows queue-length > 2000 for > 3 minutes.
2) Bridge: IC declared P1. Bridge lead creates incident with ID: INC-{{YYYYMMDD}}-### and assigns Primary Responder.
3) Quick checks (first 10 min):
   - kubectl get pods -n inference | grep inference-router && kubectl top pods --namespace=inference
   - Query /metrics for queue_length, in_flight_requests, average_latency.
   - Check upstream model-serving error-rate with grafana panel model-serving/error-rate.
4) Containment steps (apply in order):
   a) Enable request-drop policy for large batched requests (threshold: 20k tokens) via feature-flag: curl -X POST $FF_API/flags/drop-large-requests
   b) Scale inference-router deployment: kubectl scale deploy inference-router --replicas=+3
   c) If inference-router pods show OOMs, scale back and route traffic to dedicated reserve pool: admin-cli route set inference-router reserve-pool us-west-2-reserve
5) Remediation:
   - If root cause is a buggy model variant, rollback: admin-cli model rollback <model-id> --to-version <previous>
   - If root cause is corrupted cache, run selective cache flush: admin-cli cache flush --prefix user-responses-2026-*
6) Validation: watch /dashboards/request-queue and SLO panel for 30 minutes before notifying resolution.

Postmortem process (timeline & expectations):
- Within 24 hours: incident timeline (who, what, when) posted to incident document (internal).
- Within 72 hours: postmortem draft (timeline + preliminary RCA + action items) authored by Postmortem Owner.
- Within 10 business days: postmortem reviewed by stakeholders, action owners assigned and scheduled.
- Postmortem format: Title, Summary, Impact (customers, SLOs, duration), Timeline (minute-level), Root Cause(s), Contributing factors, Corrective actions (owner + due date), Preventive actions, Follow-up validation plan.
- Blamelessness reminder: focus on systemic fixes and process changes; identify gaps in metrics/observability where failure stemmed from.

Postmortem template (copy/paste):
- Title:
- Incident ID:
- Impact summary: (SLOs, percentages, affected regions/customers)
- Timeline: (chronological; include dashboard snapshots where possible)
- Root cause:
- Contributing factors:
- Corrective actions (owner, ETA, status):
- Preventive actions (owner, ETA):
- Post-deployment verification plan:
- Lessons learned and runbook updates:

On-call rotations and handoff guidance:
- Schedule cadence: primary on-call rotates weekly (Monday 08:00 -> next Monday 08:00) with a 30-minute staggered overlap on handoff days (07:30 - 08:00) for verbal sync.
- Backup policy: each primary has a named backup who must acknowledge page within 15 minutes.
- Handoff checklist:
  1) Confirm outstanding incidents assigned and current state.
  2) Review active alerts and temporary mitigations (feature flags, rollbacks).
  3) Share ongoing work that might interact with live traffic (releases, model rollouts).
  4) Confirm contact points for infra, legal, security, and CS.
- On-call fatigue mitigation: rotate critical weeks on a four-week max before a week with reduced duties; discourage late-night code pushes during on-call week unless critical.

Game day (exercise) plan — quarterly baseline test:
- Objectives: validate rollback procedures, status communications, cross-team escalations, and postmortem timeline adherence.
- Frequency: quarterly for SRE/serving/runtime teams; bi-annual for cross-functional full-org exercises.
- Participants: SRE, serving-runtime, infra, product (on-call representative), customer success (communications).
- Example scenario: simulated region failure where model-serving cluster loses 60% capacity and latencies spike > 3x.
- Success metrics: time-to-detect < 10 min, time-to-first-containment < 30 min, time-to-restoration < 90 min, postmortem draft within 72 hours.
- Scoring rubric: each role graded on checklist completion; a rolling pass/fail and explicit remediation plan required for failures.

Status page and customer communications (templates and cadence):
- Principles: fast acknowledgement, transparent status updates, avoid overpromising timelines, follow-up with RCA and customer impact details.

1) Initial customer notification (short):
Subject: Redwood Inference — Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} — Service Degradation
Body: We are investigating an issue impacting inference latency and/or availability for some customers. Our team has identified the affected components and is actively working on mitigation. We will provide an update by {{ETA_IN_MIN}} minutes. Incident ID: {{INCIDENT_ID}}.

2) Update (example at 30 minutes):
Subject: Update — Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} — Mitigation in progress
Body: We mitigated a subset of traffic by routing to alternate model variants and applied temporary request-rate controls. We continue to monitor progress. Estimated next update: {{ETA_IN_MIN}} minutes.

3) Resolution notice:
Subject: Resolved — Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}}
Body: The issue impacting inference availability has been resolved at {{RESOLUTION_TIME}}. Services have been validated against SLOs for 30 minutes. A post-incident report (RCA) will be published within 10 business days. If you experienced customer-facing issues, please respond to this message and our CS team will follow up.

4) Postmortem/customer impact summary (final):
Subject: Root cause analysis — Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}}
Body: A detailed RCA has been published: [link]. Summary: root cause, affected model versions/customers, timeline, mitigation taken, corrective actions and ETA for preventive changes.

Customer comms guidelines:
- Coordinate with Communications Lead and CS for enterprise customers before sending details beyond the status page.
- For high-impact incidents (P0), provide a dedicated customer update channel (Slack/Bridge) for affected customers with a named CS liaison.

Runbook maintenance and ownership:
- Single source of truth: all runbooks live under this space and are tagged by service.
- Owners: each runbook must list an owner and secondary owner. Owners are responsible for annual validation and post-game-day updates.
- Retirement: runbooks older than 18 months without an owner will be flagged for review and archived.

Example of runbook metadata header (required):
- Runbook name:
- Owner: (name + pager)
- Secondary: (name + pager)
- Last updated:
- Tested: (date of last game-day / simulation)
- Applicable SLOs:

Audit and continuous improvement:
- After every incident, the IC and Postmortem Owner run a 30-minute retro within 5 business days to validate action item owners and refine detection thresholds.
- Quarterly metrics: mean time to detect (MTTD), mean time to restore (MTTR), % postmortems completed on time. These numbers published to /dashboards/ops-metrics.

Appendix: quick templates and commands
- Create incident: admin-cli incident create --title "<short summary>" --severity P0 --service inference-router
- Rollback model: admin-cli model rollback <model-id> --to-version <v123> --reason "emergency rollback"
- Example status message (short):
  We are aware of elevated latency for inference requests in us-west-2. We are actively investigating. Incident ID: INC-20260214-087.

- Handoff note template (to include in rotation slack channel):
  Today I am handing off: [INC-...], temp-mitigations: [feature-flag xyz], pending tasks: [scale res pool, follow-up: storage cleanup], special notes: [no on-call deployments scheduled].

Contact matrix (primary escalation contacts):
- SRE lead: Marco Li (pager: +1-555-0103)
- Serving Runtime lead: Sofia Nguyen (pager: +1-555-0121)
- Platform Infra: Ethan Reyes (pager: +1-555-0177)
- Customer Success escalation: Priya Kaur (CS)

Notes and housekeeping:
- Keep the bridge focused: use chat for non-critical coordination; IC controls the timeline for external comms.
- Do not mark incidents resolved until SLO validation is complete for at least 30 minutes.
- Ensure postmortem includes links to dashboards and all relevant logs and traces.

End of playbook.
